# Tool reference (generated)

Every tool the assistant can call, projected straight from the live registry
(`internal/tools` as wired by `app.DefaultToolBuilder`). This file is the inventory;
[`../TOOLS.md`](../TOOLS.md) is the contributor guide for *adding* one, and the
argument schemas live in the tool definitions themselves.

**Do not edit this file.** It is regenerated from the registry and diffed in CI, so a
hand edit is reverted on the next run and a new tool that is not regenerated fails the
build. That is the point: this inventory replaced three hand-maintained lists that had
already drifted out of agreement with each other and with the binary.

## Column meanings

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Risk** | The risk class driving tier gating and confirmation (`internal/safety`). |
| **Min tier** | Lowest permission tier that may call it at all. Below this it is denied, not prompted. |
| **Confirm** | What the interactive `main` actor is asked, **with `AUTO_APPROVE` off** (the default). `typed` = a typed phrase is required (git/system); `yes` = single-key approval; `—` = runs without asking. `AUTO_APPROVE=1` suppresses the prompt for every row — it does **not** widen the tier gate, and it never applies to unattended actors. |
| **Grant** | What an **unattended** actor (watcher, timer, wake) can do. `not needed` = no confirmation is required in the first place, so no grant is consulted and the actor simply runs it. `grantable` = it needs a scoped automation grant, or it is blocked. `never` = no grant can ever authorise it, whatever its scope. |
| **Needs** | The connection whose absence makes the tool unable to do its job. `—` means it works in degraded mode — either purely local, or it degrades gracefully and reports the outage as its answer. A tool needing two connections lists the one whose absence leaves nothing to do (no terminal to read ⇒ nothing to summarize). |
| **Parallel** | `read-cohort` = may batch with a consecutive run of other read-cohort calls; `same-tool cohort` = batches only with consecutive, already-authorised calls of the same tool; `serial` = one at a time. Opt-in per tool — `serial` reads are not batched. |
| **Flag** | Env var gating registration, when one does. |

> Two rows carry a nuance a table cannot: `grant.create` is `local` risk and so shows
> no confirmation, but it raises a **typed system confirmation** when the grant it is
> minting would cover mutating work. And `user.askMultipleChoice` needs a human at a
> TTY: every unattended actor has no question surface and gets `QUESTION_NOT_INTERACTIVE`.

## Invariants this inventory is subject to

- **No tool edits project files.** `Registry.AssertSafe` rejects, at startup, any tool
  whose name contains a file-mutating fragment. Code changes are delegated to a
  *visible* agent terminal — `agentTask.spawnForEdits` directly, or
  `workflow.startWorkOnIssue`, which creates the worktree and spawns into it.
- **`daintree.call` is the raw MCP escape hatch.** System risk, never grantable, and
  deliberately exceptional — prefer a typed wrapper whenever one exists.
- **A grant is the only unattended path _for a tool that needs confirmation_.** Reads
  and local writes (`not needed` above) run unattended without one; a watcher, timer,
  or wake turn reaching a `grantable` tool without a matching grant produces a blocked
  attention item instead of an action.
- **`Needs` is documentation, never a gate.** Dispatch does not read it. A tool whose
  connection is down still runs and returns its own clean "not connected" failure —
  gating on it would block the diagnostics a disconnected user reaches for first.
